questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a German speaking country in order to improve my German skills.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, I had an Erasmus contact person on the receiving uni who could help me.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received some guidance regarding some technical things and overall questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was quite easy, I found it through
WG-gesucht.de
. You can also sign up for studierendewohnheim (kollegie) but you have to do it about half a year before you need the place.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is no on campus living, so everybody lives off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Long waiting time it you want to find something through the uni, but they were very helpful also with providing links and recommendations for finding housing on your own.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: lots of different links and webpages, but they are good at guiding.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I cannot remember exactly, but it was like going to one link filling in information, getting a paper that needed to be signed, unloading it at another page, filling in more information and so on. All in all it was a very long process I think. Maybe it's the same for all institutions. But they provide you with all the information so you just have to do it in small steps.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You get an Erasmus coordinator at the receiving uni that you can always contact per mail or call.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't have to sign up for classes myself, my erasmus coordinator did it for me.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It can seem confusing but they have step guides to help you and you can always reach out to your erasmus coordinator.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In Germany they don't have BA and MA when you study medicine, it's just one long education.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was fine, but the doctors are often busy. But it's the same in Denmark .

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Blokpraktikum innere medizin 
Blokpraktikum anestäsie

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Anestäsie was very good, innere was a little confusing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very good opportunities to play many different sport for a very low price

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Erasmus had a lot of social events, so did the international club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hochschulesport if you like doing sports

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit Köln, Maastricht, Cochem, Koblenz. Go hike in the Siebengebirge. Go bouldering. Study at the ULB. Meet friends at the rhein or Hofgarten, go to one of the manyyy cute cafés in Altstadt or Südstadt. Run with socialrun Bonn (you can find them on insta). Bonn is a great city just to chill in both your friends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy as it was not very different.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live in a WG with local students! It's not always easy as most local students already have their social circle and are not looking for new friendships. But it is definitely possible, and you can always try to ask if they want to get coffee or something. But it's also so easy to meet other (international) students, so you might not need more friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There weren't any cultural differences

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Likes to go feiern:) but the Germans are very much like the Danes.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy it!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can't think of anything right now.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know so many new nice people, getting to practice my German, trying to live in another city.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: being away from my friends, boyfriend and family. But it was only for 4 months and definitely worth it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
